title: fix(app-shell): the console asks GET /usage/storage only when the runtime serves features.storageUsage (objectui#11002)
body:
Fixes #11002
Clause-②: yes

The console asks `GET /api/v1/usage/storage` only when the runtime serves it. This applies the card's ruling `5890841811` (letter A) as written. The cloud distribution serves `features.storageUsage: true` exactly when its composition mounts the endpoint plugin. That half landed through objectstack-ai/cloud#2517, and cloud `main` `2205b53` derives it from the plugin list. This side reads the flag default-off, through one boolean that both banners share.

## What publishes (`@object-ui/app-shell`, `minor`)

- **Type (the Clause-② widening).** The exported `RuntimeFeatures` gains one optional member, `storageUsage?: boolean`. `AppShellRuntimeConfig.features`, and the value `getRuntimeConfig()` returns, carry it too.
- **Value.** It is `false` by default, and after any runtime-config payload whose `features.storageUsage` is not the literal `true`. Absent, `false`, `'true'` and `1` all read as `false`; only `true` reads as `true`. As with every feature key, a payload with no `features` object leaves the current value.
- **Behaviour of the exported `ConsoleShell`.** Its two banners request the endpoint only when the viewer is the environment admin, as before, and the flag is on. Both read the same flag and still share one request. A cloud runtime older than cloud#2517 sends no key, so its admins see neither banner until that runtime is upgraded.
- **Not published.** The accessor `isStorageUsageServed()` is module-internal, like `isMarketplaceEnabled()` and `isAiStudioEnabled()`. It ships inside `dist/` but is not on the package entry, and the `exports` map has only `.` and `./styles.css`. Measured: the package entry re-exports neither the two banners nor `useStorageUsageReading` / `useReadRateReading`. The hooks are unchanged and keep their `enabled = true` default.
- No export is added or removed, and no existing member changes type. The changeset says the same.

## Changes

- `runtime-config.ts`:
  - the new `RuntimeFeatures.storageUsage` member, with a docblock in its siblings' voice;
  - `storageUsage: false` in the defaults;
  - `storageUsage: body.features.storageUsage === true` in `initRuntimeConfig`, beside `customDomain` / `sso` / `scim`;
  - `isStorageUsageServed()`, which fails closed (`=== true`) and reads `features?.`. Its docblock records why: the opposite direction from the marketplace and AI Studio accessors, and never inferred from a 404.
- `StorageUsageBanner` and `ReadRateBanner`: each passes `enabled: isAdmin && isStorageUsageServed()` and says so in its module header.
- `ConsoleShell.tsx`:
  - the two mount comments name the second gate;
  - the stale comment that called `useDiscovery()` the AI chatbot's gate now names the readers that exist. `useViewData` and `useElementDataSource` fall back to `SchemaRendererContext`'s `dataSource`. Measured: nothing in product source calls `useDiscovery`.
- `packages/app-shell/README.md` (Storage capacity section) and `content/docs/guide/console.md` (the feature-flag list).

The gate sits in the banners, not the hooks. The hooks are generic readers that already take `enabled`; whether the shell's banner should ask is a fact about where the shell mounts it.

## Reproduction (red at base `278d244`)

The new `ConsoleShell.storageUsageGate-11002.test.tsx` mounts the real `ConsoleShell`, fills the real runtime-config singleton through `initRuntimeConfig`, and uses the real shared endpoint reader. Only `useWorkspaceAdminStatus` and the network are stood in. Run against the base code it reads `Tests 2 failed | 2 passed (4)`. The no-key and `false` cases fail with `expected [ '/api/v1/usage/storage' ] to have a length of +0 but got 1`. At base, the served case already shared ONE request between the two banners: that was measured here, not assumed.

## Pins

- `ConsoleShell.storageUsageGate-11002.test.tsx`:
  - an admin with no `storageUsage` key issues zero requests, and so does an admin with `storageUsage: false`;
  - an admin with `storageUsage: true` issues exactly one request, shared by both banners. The storage banner renders `data-storage-usage-case="warning"` on the `warn` verdict, and the read-rate banner renders on the same response;
  - a non-admin with `storageUsage: true` issues zero requests.
  - Each zero is read after the same settle that sees the one request in the served case.
- `runtime-config.test.ts`, describe `runtime-config storageUsage (objectui#11002)`:
  - off before init;
  - on for the literal `true`;
  - off for absent, `false`, `'true'` and `1`;
  - off when the config fetch fails;
  - withdrawn when a later fetch no longer serves it.

## Ablations

Every mutation went through objectstack's `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`. The anchor hit once and was gone afterwards, and the blob hash changed. Each restore was proven by blob == HEAD and an empty `git diff HEAD`, all from committed state.

| mutation | went red | stayed green |
| --- | --- | --- |
| drop the mapping line | `is ON when the server sends the literal true`, `withdraws it when a later fetch no longer serves it`, the shell's ONE-request case (3 failed) | the falsy-input pins: the default is already `false`, so a dropped line cannot turn them |
| mapping `=== true` changed to `!!` | `is OFF when the key is the string 'true'`, `... the number 1` (2 failed) | the rest |
| drop the gate in `StorageUsageBanner` | the shell's no-key and `false` cases, 1 request each (2 failed) | the served and non-admin cases |
| drop the gate in `ReadRateBanner` | the same two (2 failed) | the same two |
| drop `isAdmin &&` in `StorageUsageBanner` | the non-admin case (1 failed) | the other three |

**Reverse check of the published type.** After `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell build`, `dist/runtime-config.d.ts` carries `storageUsage?: boolean`, and `dist/index.d.ts` names `RuntimeFeatures` with no `isStorageUsageServed`. A scratch probe resolved `@object-ui/app-shell` to that built `index.d.ts` (deleted after use):
- `RuntimeFeatures['storageUsage'] = true` compiled (exit 0);
- `= 'yes'` failed with `TS2322: Type '"yes"' is not assignable to type 'boolean | undefined'` (exit 2).

## Gates

**What the lint run covers.** The population is the six changed source and test files, linted under the root `eslint.config.js`, and the JSON output counts six. The narrowing is safe: the config enables no type-aware linting (no `projectService` and no `parserOptions.project`), and no local rule in `eslint-rules/` reads the filesystem. So this diff cannot change a verdict on an untouched file. The repo-wide `pnpm lint` belongs to CI.

**The touched-suites run** was selected two ways: by import (the importers of `runtime-config.ts`, the two banners and `ConsoleShell.tsx` sit in `console/`, `layout/`, `chrome/` and `observability/`), and by source-text read (a grep for `readFileSync`, `?raw` and the file names). The full-package run covers both.

## Acceptance notes

- `StorageUsageBanner.test.tsx` and `ReadRateBanner.test.tsx` mock their hook. Their admin cases now hand the mock `enabled: false`, because the runtime-config default is off, and the mock answers with a reading anyway. They stay green and test the classifier, not the gate. The shell pins above test the gate. carrier: none.
- `isStorageUsageServed()` is read at render, like `isAiStudioEnabled()`, and the console awaits `initRuntimeConfig` before the first render. A later re-init does not re-render the banners by itself. That is unchanged sibling behaviour, not a new gap. carrier: none.
